newsitem.title: CANADA: Alcan says volumes, prices hurt results.
newsitem.headline: Alcan says volumes, prices hurt results.

text.p: Alcan Aluminium Ltd said on Thursday its profitability in the third quarter was adversely impacted by lower volumes and lower primary prices.

"Further customer destocking in the U.S., seasonal slowing in Europe and increased competition in export markets led volumes to slip from second quarter levels," said Alcan president and chief executive Jacques Bougie.
"This, together with the fallout from substantially lower primary prices, had an adverse impact on profitability."

Alcan reported today a profit of US$0.43 per share in the third quarter of 1996 compared to a loss of US$0.63 per share after a US$420 million writedown in the same period a year earlier. Revenues for the third quarter were down to US$1.88 billion from US$2.29 billion a year earlier.
Bougie said Alcan sees a stable outlook in North America and improving conditions in Europe.
"On a positive note, we are now seeing some early signs of improvement in Europe and business conditions in North America remain stable, particularly in the non-can sheet sectors," Bougie said.
